name: Ferrex-NT
description: Ferrex-NT is an iron-nickel-chromium alloy with a quantum-engineered band structure that exploits quantum tunneling at macroscopic scale — specifically, its electron transport properties allow current to tunnel through normally insulating barrier layers within composite structures, eliminating contact resistance at metal-ceramic or metal-polymer interfaces. This makes Ferrex-NT uniquely valuable as a bridge material in hybrid composites where conventional conductors would fail at material boundaries. Secondary properties include an anomalous Hall effect at room temperature usable for solid-state magnetic sensing with no moving parts.
story_hooks: BioForge Labs has been quietly purchasing Ferrex-NT through shell buyers to develop a new SNT interface that bypasses standard neural handshake protocols — the resulting implant would give them direct read access to connected nervous systems without the user's knowledge.

A Ferrex-NT shipment designated for a military prosthetics program was rerouted to an unlicensed fabricator in the mid-tiers — the fabricator is producing unauthorized neural contact implants and selling them cheap, but the quantum tunneling properties are doing something unexpected in human tissue.

The anomalous Hall effect in a Ferrex-NT sensor array is picking up a magnetic field pattern that doesn't correspond to any known installation or geological feature — it's consistent, it's regular, and it's moving slowly upward through the city.
